taxonomyNote: NatureServe uses Eastern Copperhead and recognizes no subspecies; Animal Diversity Web names it Southern Copperhead.
fieldMarks: Reddish-brown body with tan, copper and rich brown crossbands
Juveniles greyer with a yellow-tinted tail tip until about age 3-4
behavior: Diurnal in spring and fall, mostly nocturnal in summer
Active about April to October/November in the north; hibernates communally in rocky dens or burrows
Sit-and-wait feeder on small mammals, snakes, lizards, amphibians, insects and small birds
May migrate several hundred metres between winter den and summer range
habitat: Deciduous forest with rock outcrops, floodplains and swamp edges; often with rocks, logs, stumps or leaf litter as cover.
range: Southern New England to northern Florida, west through the southern Great Lakes states and southern Iowa to southeastern Nebraska, eastern Kansas, eastern Oklahoma and eastern Texas. Not a Canadian species.

lookalikes.name: Water snakes and cottonmouth
lookalikes.howToTell: Animal Diversity Web notes they resemble copperheads but differ in pattern and behaviour.
